title: Transfinite Mathematics
description: Cantor proved that some infinities are bigger than others. Build them. Unlocks the Cantor Diagonalizer.

puzzle.goal: A finite set S has n elements. Its subsets can be counted by size: there are 'n choose j' subsets with exactly j elements. The set of all subsets is itself a set, whose subsets can be counted the same way. Write how many more subsets the set of all subsets has than S itself has, counting both by size.
puzzle.name: Cantor's theorem for finite sets (power-set cardinality)
puzzle.form: sum ( k , 0 , sum ( j , 0 , n , binom ( n , j ) ) , binom ( sum ( j , 0 , n , binom ( n , j ) ) , k ) ) - sum ( j , 0 , n , binom ( n , j ) )
puzzle.ask: Each sum is a binomial expansion of (1 + 1)^m = 2^m. Find N for a 4-element set.

vars.j: size of a subset of S
vars.k: size of a subset of the power set

puzzle.method: Count subsets by their size with binomial coefficients; the inner count is the size of the power set, which becomes the n of the outer count.
